title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Law Reporter Shelf. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Reporter Shelf
options.lineage: West's Pacific Reporter volumes on a law-library shelf
options.thesis: Every evaluation is a bound volume; the cohort is a shelf, and your judge's spine is pulled out of line.
options.viewport: Buckram top bar with county select; your 2026 ballot as ranked rows, each led by its spine and a shelf strip placing it among all peers.
options.risk: Legal-world gold-on-dark can tip into law-firm pomp if foil is used anywhere but rank numerals.

raised.raise: One fixed percentile ramp: shelf position, bar length and tint mean the same thing in every view.
Every derived number sits next to the source figure and a link to the state PDF it came from.
One text size does the body and table work; hierarchy comes from weight and the spine labels.
Every evaluation carries a citation-style identifier (2026 Colo. JPE 20th Dist.) used in URLs and tables.

options.label: The Blue Book
options.lineage: Colorado's State Ballot Information Booklet, mailed to every household
options.thesis: Read like the booklet already on the voter's kitchen table: numbered entries, two sober columns, one deep blue.
options.viewport: Booklet-blue header band, county select, judges as numbered entries with a score ruler under each name.
options.risk: Familiar civic-document look; this is where most voter-guide runs land.

options.label: Pass and Board
options.lineage: boarding passes and airport gate boards
options.thesis: Each judge gets a segmented pass of labeled numbers; the cohort is a board ranked by composite.
options.viewport: Board of your ballot's judges ranked by composite; tapping one opens its segmented pass.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and segments are very scannable; loses on identification, voters don't read a ballot as travel.
options.risk: Travel metaphor (gates, boarding) has nothing to say about judges.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: Rankings as a departure board whose flaps cascade on sort.
options.viewport: Black board, ranked judge rows in white caps.
options.case: Loses both: no voter identification, and flap motion adds nothing a table lacks.
options.kept: Columns never move; only values change, so sorting never reflows the grid.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Judges as stars, magnitude as score.
options.case: Loses both: dot area is a weak encoding for close scores.
options.kept: A single fixed magnitude ramp shared by every view.

options.label: Monochrome Proof
options.thesis: Claim paired with proof, one accent.
options.case: Loses both: a sales page grammar for a reference tool.
options.kept: Every claim sits beside its proof.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Courts as coloured tab divisions sized by extent.
options.case: Loses both: heavy material system for a lookup task.
options.kept: One text size does the work.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.case: Loses both: hiding names is the opposite of a voter's need.
options.kept: Every artifact carries a catalog number.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A nonpartisan voter guide, executed impeccably: white, civic blue, judge cards with score badges.
canonCard.viewport: Address or county search, then a card per judge with a score badge and recommendation chip.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other voter guide by design.
